The CPU core is heavily parametrizable and well suited for 10: embedded control applications. Ibex is being extensively verified and has 11: seen multiple tape-outs. Ibex supports the Integer (I) or Embedded (E), 12: Integer Multiplication and Division (M), Compressed (C), and B (Bit 13: Manipulation) extensions. 14: 15:

16: 17: Ibex was initially developed as part of the [PULP platform](https://www.pulp-platform.org) 18: under the name ["Zero-riscy"](https://doi.org/10.1109/PATMOS.2017.8106976), and has been 19: contributed to [lowRISC](https://www.lowrisc.org) who maintains it and develops it further. It is 20: under active development. 21: 22: ## Configuration 23: 24: Ibex offers several configuration parameters to meet the needs of various application scenarios. 25: The options include different choices for the architecture of the multiplier unit, as well as a range of performance and security features. 26: The table below indicates performance, area and verification status for a few selected configurations. 27: These are configurations on which lowRISC is focusing for performance evaluation and design verification (see [supported configs](ibex_configs.yaml)). 28: 29: | Config | "micro" | "small" | "maxperf" | "maxperf-pmp-bmfull" | 30: | ------ | ------- | --------| ----------| -------------------- | 31: | Features | RV32EC | RV32IMC, 3 cycle mult | RV32IMC, 1 cycle mult, Branch target ALU, Writeback stage | RV32IMCB, 1 cycle mult, Branch target ALU, Writeback stage, 16 PMP regions | 32: | Performance (CoreMark/MHz) | 0.904 | 2.47 | 3.13 | 3.13 | 33: | Area - Yosys (kGE) | 16.85 | 26.60 | 32.48 | 66.02 | 34: | Area - Commercial (estimated kGE) | ~15 | ~24 | ~30 | ~61 | 35: | Verification status | Red | Green | Green | Green | 36: 37: Notes: 38: 39: * Performance numbers are based on CoreMark running on the Ibex Simple System [platform](examples/simple_system/README.md). 40: Note that different ISAs (use of B and C extensions) give the best results for different configurations. 41: See the [Benchmarks README](examples/sw/benchmarks/README.md) for more information. 42: * Yosys synthesis area numbers are based on the Ibex basic synthesis [flow](syn/README.md) using the latch-based register file. 43: * Commercial synthesis area numbers are a rough estimate of what might be achievable with a commercial synthesis flow and technology library. 44: * For comparison, the original "Zero-riscy" core yields an area of 23.14kGE using our Yosys synthesis flow. 45: * Verification status is a rough guide to the overall maturity of a particular configuration. 46: Green indicates that verification is close to complete. 47: Amber indicates that some verification has been performed, but the configuration is still experimental. 48: Red indicates a configuration with minimal/no verification. 49: Users must make their own assessment of verification readiness for any tapeout. 50: * v.1.0.0 of the RISC-V Bit-Manipulation Extension is supported as well as the remaining sub-extensions of draft v.0.93 of the bitmanip spec. 51: The latter are *not ratified* and there may be changes before ratification. 52: See [Standards Compliance](https://ibex-core.readthedocs.io/en/latest/01_overview/compliance.html) in the Ibex documentation for more information. 53: 54: ## Documentation 55: 56: The Ibex user manual can be 57: [read online at ReadTheDocs](https://ibex-core.readthedocs.io/en/latest/). It is also contained in 58: the `doc` folder of this repository. 59: 60: ## Examples 61: 62: The Ibex repository includes [Simple System](examples/simple_system/README.md). 63: This is an intentionally simple integration of Ibex with a basic system that targets simulation. 64: It is intended to provide an easy way to get bare metal binaries running on Ibex in simulation. 65: 66: A more complete example can be found in the [Ibex Demo System repository](https://github.com/lowrisc/ibex-demo-system). 67: In particular it includes a integration of the [PULP RISC-V debug module](https://github.com/pulp-platform/riscv-dbg). 68: It targets the [Arty A7 FPGA board from Digilent](https://digilent.com/shop/arty-a7-artix-7-fpga-development-board/) and supports debugging via OpenOCD and GDB over USB (no external JTAG probe required). 69: The Ibex Demo System is maintained by lowRISC but is not an official part of Ibex. 70: 71: ## Contributing 72: 73: We highly appreciate community contributions. 1: Ibex simulation Control/Status Registers Testbench
2: ==================================================
3: 
4: This directory contains a basic sample testbench in C++ for testing correctness of some CS registers implemented in Ibex.
5: 
6: It is a work in progress and only tests a handful of registers, and is missing many features.
7: 
8: How to build and run the testbench
9: ----------------------------------
10: 
11: Verilator version:
12: 
13:    ```sh
14:    fusesoc --cores-root=. run --target=sim --tool=verilator lowrisc:ibex:tb_cs_registers
15:    ```
16: VCS version:
17: 
18:    ```sh
19:    fusesoc --cores-root=. run --target=sim --tool=vcs lowrisc:ibex:tb_cs_registers
20:    ```
21: 
22: Testbench file structure
23: ------------------------
24: 
25: `tb/tb_cs_registers.sv` - Is the verilog top level, it instantiates the DUT and DPI calls
26: 
27: `tb/tb_cs_registers.cc` - Is the C++ top level, it sets up the testbench components
28: 
29: `driver/` - Contains components to generate and drive random register transactions
30: 
31: `env/` - Contains components to generate and drive other signals
32: 
33: `model/` - Contains a model of the register state and checking functions
34: 
35: DPI methodology
36: ---------------
37: 
38: The testbench relies on DPI calls to interface between the RTL and the C++ driver/checker components.
39: This methodology allows the testbench to support both Verilator and commercial simulators.
40: 
41: Each DPI call has a function in SV (which is called in the SV top-level), and a corresponding C function.
42: To support the instantiation of multiple instances of TB components, some DPI modules can register their objects referenced by name.
43: Each DPI call from the RTL then calls into the correct instance by matching the name.
44: 
45: Testbench structure
46: -------------------
47: 
48: The driver component contains one DPI "interface" to drive new random transactions into the DUT, and another to monitor issued transactions including the DUT's responses.
49: Each time a new transaction is detected by the monitor component, it is captured and sent to the model.
50: The model reads incoming transactions, updates its internal state and checks that the DUT outputs matches its own predictions.
51: 

(End of file - total 51 lines)
</content>

14:   // Instantiate all the registers
15:   for (unsigned int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
16:     uint32_t reg_addr = 0x3A0 + i;
17:     if (params->PMPEnable && (i < (params->PMPNumRegions / 4))) {
18:       register_map_.push_back(
19:           std::make_unique<PmpCfgRegister>(reg_addr, &register_map_));
20:     } else {

23:     }

26:     uint32_t reg_addr = 0x3B0 + i;

28:       register_map_.push_back(
29:           std::make_unique<PmpAddrRegister>(reg_addr, &register_map_));
30:     } else {
31:       register_map_.push_back(
32:           std::make_unique<NonImpRegister>(reg_addr, &register_map_));
33:     }
34:   }
35:   // mcountinhibit
36:   // - MSBs are always 0: unused counters cannot be inhibited
37:   // - Bit 1 is always 0: time cannot be disabled
38:   uint32_t mcountinhibit_mask =
39:       (~((0x1 << params->MHPMCounterNum) - 1) << 3) | 0x2;
40:   uint32_t mcountinhibit_resval = 0;
41:   register_map_.push_back(std::make_unique<WARLRegister>(
42:       0x320, &register_map_, mcountinhibit_mask, mcountinhibit_resval));
43:   // Performance counter setup
44:   for (unsigned int i = 3; i < 32; i++) {
45:     uint32_t reg_addr = 0x320 + i;

61:   uint32_t mhpmcounter_mask_low, mhpmcounter_mask_high;

1: // Copyright lowRISC contributors.
2: // Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0, see LICENSE for details.
3: // SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
4: 
5: /*******************************************************************************
6:  * Directed test to check data independent timing feature
7:  *
8:  * This test uses a couple of functions, `count_ones_zeros` and `div_ones_zero`
9:  * that exhibit data dependent timing. This is via branch instructions in
10:  * `count_one_zeros` and via divide instructions in `div_ones_zeros`, which are
11:  * the only two types of instruction with data dependent timing in Ibex.
12:  *
13:  * The rest runs multiple iterations of each function providing input from an
14:  * LFSR, timing each iteration. The test passes where at least 25% of run times
15:  * differ for each function when data independent timing is disabled and where
16:  * all run times are identical for each function when data independent timing is
17:  * enabled.
18:  *
19:  * It does a second run with data independent timing enabled and the ICache
20:  * enabled. This time the functions must be called once with their timing result
21:  * discarded to warm up the ICache. With that done the function iterations must
22:  * exhibit identical timing as before for the test to pass.
23:  * ****************************************************************************/
24: 
25: #include "simple_system_common.h"
26: 
27: extern uint32_t count_ones_zeros(uint32_t n);
28: extern uint32_t div_ones_zeros(uint32_t n);
29: 
30: #define LFSR_POLY 0x80000057
31: #define NUM_ITERATIONS 100
32: #define INITIAL_VAL 0xDEADBEEF
33: 
34: // Simple LFSR step function
35: uint32_t next_val(uint32_t cur_val) {
36:   uint32_t bottom_bit = cur_val & 0x1;
37:   cur_val >>= 1;
38: 
39:   if (bottom_bit) {
40:     cur_val ^= LFSR_POLY;
41:   }
42: 
43:   return cur_val;
44: }
45: 
46: // Enable/disable data independent timing
47: void set_dit(uint32_t on) {
48:   if (on) {
49:     __asm__ volatile("csrsi 0x7c0, 0x2");
50:   } else {
51:     __asm__ volatile("csrci 0x7c0, 0x2");
52:   }
53: }
54: 
55: // Enable/disable ICache
56: void set_icache(uint32_t on) {
57:   if (on) {
58:     __asm__ volatile("csrsi 0x7c0, 0x1");
59:   } else {
60:     __asm__ volatile("csrci 0x7c0, 0x1");
61:   }
62: }
63: 
64: // Run NUM_ITERATIONS of count_ones_zeros noting the cycle time from each.
65: // Return how many times one iteration differed in cycle time from the next.
66: uint32_t test_b_run_time() {
67:   uint32_t val = INITIAL_VAL;
68:   uint32_t mismatches = 0;
69:   uint32_t last_cycles = count_ones_zeros(val);
70: 
71:   for (int i = 0; i < NUM_ITERATIONS; ++i) {
72:     val = next_val(val);
73: 
74:     uint32_t cycles = count_ones_zeros(val);
75:     if (cycles != last_cycles) {
76:       ++mismatches;
77:     }
78: 
79:     last_cycles = cycles;
80:   }
81: 
82:   return mismatches;
83: }
84: 
85: // Run NUM_ITERATIONS of div_ones_zeros noting the cycle time from each.
86: // Return how many times one iteration differed in cycle time from the next.
87: uint32_t test_div_run_time() {
88:   uint32_t val = INITIAL_VAL;
89:   uint32_t mismatches = 0;
90:   uint32_t last_cycles = div_ones_zeros(val);
91: 
92:   for (int i = 0; i < NUM_ITERATIONS; ++i) {
93:     val = next_val(val);
94: 
95:     uint32_t cycles = div_ones_zeros(val);
96:     if (cycles != last_cycles) {
97:       ++mismatches;
98:     }
99: 
100:     last_cycles = cycles;
101:   }
102: 
103:   return mismatches;
104: }
105: 
106: int main(void) {
107:   uint32_t mismatches;
108:   pcount_enable(1);
109: 
110:   set_dit(0);
111:   mismatches = test_b_run_time();
112:   if (mismatches < (NUM_ITERATIONS / 4)) {
113:     puts(
114:         "FAILURE: Too few cycle mismatches seen for branch test when DIT "
115:         "disabled: 0x");
116:     puthex(mismatches);
117:     return 1;
118:   }
119: 
120:   set_dit(1);
121:   mismatches = test_b_run_time();
122:   if (mismatches != 0) {
123:     puts("FAILURE: Cycle mismatches seen for branch test when DIT enabled: 0x");
124:     puthex(mismatches);
125:     return 1;
126:   }
127: 
128:   set_icache(1);
129:   // Warm up ICache
130:   test_b_run_time();
131: 
132:   // Run test with ICache enabled
133:   mismatches = test_b_run_time();
134:   if (mismatches != 0) {
135:     puts(
136:         "FAILURE: Cycle mismatches seen for branch test when DIT and ICache "
137:         "enabled: 0x");
138:     puthex(mismatches);
139:     return 1;
140:   }
141: 
142:   set_icache(0);
143: 
144:   set_dit(0);
145:   mismatches = test_div_run_time();
146:   if (mismatches < (NUM_ITERATIONS / 4)) {
147:     puts(
148:         "FAILURE: Too few cycle mismatches seen for divide test when DIT "
149:         "disabled: 0x");
150:     puthex(mismatches);
151:     return 1;
152:   }
153: 
154:   set_dit(1);
155:   mismatches = test_div_run_time();
156:   if (mismatches != 0) {
157:     puts("FAILURE: Cycle mismatches seen for divide test when DIT enabled: 0x");
158:     puthex(mismatches);
159:     return 1;
160:   }
161: 
162:   set_icache(1);
163:   // Warm up ICache
164:   test_div_run_time();
165: 
166:   // Run test with ICache enabled
167:   mismatches = test_div_run_time();
168:   if (mismatches != 0) {
169:     puts(
170:         "FAILURE: Cycle mismatches seen for divide test when DIT and ICache "
171:         "enabled: 0x");
172:     puthex(mismatches);
173:     return 1;
174:   }
175: 
176:   puts("PASS: All test sequences behaved as expected");

5: /*******************************************************************************
6:  * Directed test to check dummy instruction insertion feature
7:  *
8:  * This test uses a function `busy_work` which does some computation based on 3
9:  * input uint32_t arrays writing a result into a uint32_t output array.
10:  * `busy_work` is run over multiple iterations, timing each. The function does
11:  * not exhibit data dependent timing behaviour so the test passes when every run
12:  * takes an identical time with dummy instruction insertion disabled and every
13:  * run takes a different time with dummy instruction insertion enabled.
14:  ******************************************************************************/
15: 
16: #include "simple_system_common.h"
17: 
18: extern uint32_t busy_work(uint32_t num_vals, uint32_t *in_1, uint32_t *in_2,
19:                           uint32_t *in_3, uint32_t *out);
20: 
21: #define LFSR_POLY 0x80000057
22: #define INITIAL_VAL 0xDEADBEEF
23: 
24: #define NUM_VALUES 100
25: #define NUM_ITERATIONS 5
26: 
27: uint32_t next_val(uint32_t cur_val) {
28:   uint32_t bottom_bit = cur_val & 0x1;
29:   cur_val >>= 1;
30: 
31:   if (bottom_bit) {
32:     cur_val ^= LFSR_POLY;
33:   }
34: 
35:   return cur_val;
36: }
37: 
38: uint32_t lfsr_value = INITIAL_VAL;
39: 
40: void set_dummy_instr(uint32_t on) {
41:   if (on) {
42:     __asm__ volatile("csrsi 0x7c0, 0x4");
43:   } else {
44:     __asm__ volatile("csrci 0x7c0, 0x4");
45:   }
46: }
47: 
48: uint32_t in_1[100];
49: uint32_t in_2[100];
50: uint32_t in_3[100];
51: uint32_t out[100];
52: 
53: void setup_values() {
54:   for (int i = 0; i < NUM_VALUES; ++i) {
55:     in_1[i] = lfsr_value;
56:     lfsr_value = next_val(lfsr_value);
57:     in_2[i] = lfsr_value;
58:     lfsr_value = next_val(lfsr_value);
59:     in_3[i] = lfsr_value;
60:     lfsr_value = next_val(lfsr_value);
61:   }
62: }
63: 
64: uint32_t run_busy_work_test(uint32_t iterations) {
65:   uint32_t last_cycles;
66:   uint32_t mismatches = 0;
67: 
68:   setup_values();
69:   last_cycles = busy_work(NUM_VALUES, in_1, in_2, in_3, out);
70:   for (int i = 0; i < iterations - 1; ++i) {
71:     uint32_t cycles = busy_work(NUM_VALUES, in_1, in_2, in_3, out);
72: 
73:     if (cycles != last_cycles) {
74:       mismatches++;
75:     }
76: 
77:     last_cycles = cycles;
78:   }
79: 
80:   return mismatches;
81: }
82: 
83: int main(void) {
84:   uint32_t mismatches;
85:   pcount_enable(1);
86: 
87:   set_dummy_instr(0);
88:   mismatches = run_busy_work_test(NUM_ITERATIONS);
89:   if (mismatches != 0) {

91:     puthex(mismatches);

101:     puthex(mismatches);
102:     return 1;
103:   }
104:

5: /**
6:  * Simplistic Ibex bus implementation
7:  *
8:  * This module is designed for demo and simulation purposes, do not use it in
9:  * a real-world system.
10:  *
11:  * This implementation doesn't handle the full bus protocol, but makes the
12:  * following simplifying assumptions.
13:  *
14:  * - All devices (slaves) must respond in the next cycle after the request.
15:  * - Host (master) arbitration is strictly priority based.
16:  */
17: module bus #(
18:   parameter int NrDevices    = 1,
19:   parameter int NrHosts      = 1,
20:   parameter int DataWidth    = 32,
21:   parameter int AddressWidth = 32
22: ) (
23:   input                           clk_i,
24:   input                           rst_ni,
25: 
26:   // Hosts (masters)
27:   input                           host_req_i    [NrHosts],
28:   output logic                    host_gnt_o    [NrHosts],
29: 
30:   input        [AddressWidth-1:0] host_addr_i   [NrHosts],
31:   input                           host_we_i     [NrHosts],
32:   input        [ DataWidth/8-1:0] host_be_i     [NrHosts],
33:   input        [   DataWidth-1:0] host_wdata_i  [NrHosts],
34:   output logic                    host_rvalid_o [NrHosts],
35:   output logic [   DataWidth-1:0] host_rdata_o  [NrHosts],
36:   output logic                    host_err_o    [NrHosts],
37: 
38:   // Devices (slaves)
39:   output logic                    device_req_o    [NrDevices],
40: 
41:   output logic [AddressWidth-1:0] device_addr_o   [NrDevices],
42:   output logic                    device_we_o     [NrDevices],
43:   output logic [ DataWidth/8-1:0] device_be_o     [NrDevices],
44:   output logic [   DataWidth-1:0] device_wdata_o  [NrDevices],
45:   input                           device_rvalid_i [NrDevices],
46:   input        [   DataWidth-1:0] device_rdata_i  [NrDevices],
47:   input                           device_err_i    [NrDevices],
48: 
49:   // Device address map
50:   input        [AddressWidth-1:0] cfg_device_addr_base [NrDevices],
51:   input        [AddressWidth-1:0] cfg_device_addr_mask [NrDevices]
52: );
53: 
54:   localparam int unsigned NumBitsHostSel = NrHosts > 1 ? $clog2(NrHosts) : 1;
55:   localparam int unsigned NumBitsDeviceSel = NrDevices > 1 ? $clog2(NrDevices) : 1;
56: 
57:   logic host_sel_valid;
58:   logic device_sel_valid;
59:   logic decode_err_resp;
60: 
61:   logic [NumBitsHostSel-1:0] host_sel_req, host_sel_resp;
62:   logic [NumBitsDeviceSel-1:0] device_sel_req, device_sel_resp;
63: 
64:   // Master select priority arbiter
65:   always_comb begin
66:     host_sel_valid = 1'b0;
67:     host_sel_req = '0;
68:     for (integer host = NrHosts - 1; host >= 0; host = host - 1) begin
69:       if (host_req_i[host]) begin
70:         host_sel_valid = 1'b1;
71:         host_sel_req = NumBitsHostSel'(host);
72:       end
73:     end
74:   end
75: 
76:   // Device select
77:   always_comb begin
78:     device_sel_valid = 1'b0;
79:     device_sel_req = '0;
80:     for (integer device = 0; device < NrDevices; device = device + 1) begin
81:       if ((host_addr_i[host_sel_req] & cfg_device_addr_mask[device])
82:           == cfg_device_addr_base[device]) begin
83:         device_sel_valid = 1'b1;
84:         device_sel_req = NumBitsDeviceSel'(device);
85:       end
86:     end
87:   end
88: 
89:   always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
90:      if (!rst_ni) begin
91:         host_sel_resp <= '0;
92:         device_sel_resp <= '0;
93:         decode_err_resp <= 1'b0;
94:      end else begin
95:         // Responses are always expected 1 cycle after the request
96:         device_sel_resp <= device_sel_req;
97:         host_sel_resp <= host_sel_req;
98:         // Decode failed; no device matched?
99:         decode_err_resp <= host_sel_valid & !device_sel_valid;
100:      end
101:   end
102: 
103:   always_comb begin
104:     for (integer device = 0; device < NrDevices; device = device + 1) begin
105:       if (device_sel_valid && NumBitsDeviceSel'(device) == device_sel_req) begin
106:         device_req_o[device]   = host_req_i[host_sel_req];
107:         device_we_o[device]    = host_we_i[host_sel_req];
108:         device_addr_o[device]  = host_addr_i[host_sel_req];
109:         device_wdata_o[device] = host_wdata_i[host_sel_req];
110:         device_be_o[device]    = host_be_i[host_sel_req];
111:       end else begin
112:         device_req_o[device]   = 1'b0;
113:         device_we_o[device]    = 1'b0;
114:         device_addr_o[device]  = 'b0;
115:         device_wdata_o[device] = 'b0;
116:         device_be_o[device]    = 'b0;
117:       end
118:     end
119:   end
120: 
121:   always_comb begin
122:     for (integer host = 0; host < NrHosts; host = host + 1) begin
123:       host_gnt_o[host] = 1'b0;
124:       if (NumBitsHostSel'(host) == host_sel_resp) begin
125:         host_rvalid_o[host] = device_rvalid_i[device_sel_resp] | decode_err_resp;
126:         host_err_o[host]    = device_err_i[device_sel_resp]    | decode_err_resp;

67:     assign mtimecmph_wdata[(b*8)+:8] = timer_be_i[b] ? timer_wdata_i[b*8+:8] :
68:                                                        mtimecmp_q[DataWidth+(b*8)+:8];

73:   assign mtimeh_we    = timer_we & (timer_addr_i[ADDR_OFFSET-1:0] == MTIME_HIGH);
74:   assign mtimecmp_we  = timer_we & (timer_addr_i[ADDR_OFFSET-1:0] == MTIMECMP_LOW);
75:   assign mtimecmph_we = timer_we & (timer_addr_i[ADDR_OFFSET-1:0] == MTIMECMP_HIGH);

77:   // Generate next data
78:   assign mtime_d    = {(mtimeh_we    ? mtimeh_wdata    : mtime_inc[63:32]),
79:                        (mtime_we     ? mtime_wdata     : mtime_inc[31:0])};
80:   assign mtimecmp_d = {(mtimecmph_we ? mtimecmph_wdata : mtimecmp_q[63:32]),
81:                        (mtimecmp_we  ? mtimecmp_wdata  : mtimecmp_q[31:0])};

83:   // Generate registers
84:   always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
85:     if (~rst_ni) begin

87:     end else begin
88:       mtime_q <= mtime_d;
89:     end
90:   end
91: 
92:   always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
93:     if (~rst_ni) begin
94:       mtimecmp_q <= 'b0;
95:     end else if (mtimecmp_we | mtimecmph_we) begin
96:       mtimecmp_q <= mtimecmp_d;
97:     end
98:   end
99: 
100:   // interrupt remains set until mtimecmp is written
101:   assign interrupt_d  = ((mtime_q >= mtimecmp_q) | interrupt_q) & ~(mtimecmp_we | mtimecmph_we);
102: 
103:   always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
104:     if (~rst_ni) begin
105:       interrupt_q <= 'b0;

109:   end

114:   always_comb begin
115:     rdata_d = 'b0;
116:     error_d = 1'b0;

119:       MTIME_HIGH:    rdata_d = mtime_q[63:32];
120:       MTIMECMP_LOW:  rdata_d = mtimecmp_q[31:0];

127:     endcase

6:  * Module for communicating with the simulator that interfaces via the memory
7:  * system.
8:  *
9:  * Contains two registers

11:  * * 0x0 - CHAR_OUT_ADDR - [7:0] of write data output via output_char DPI call
12:  * and SimOutputManager (see dv/common/cpp/sim_output_manager.cc)
13:  *
14:  * * 0x8 - SIM_CTRL_ADDR - Write 1 to bit 0 to halt sim
15:  *
16:  * The slightly odd spacing is because we also use SIM_CTRL_ADDR when
17:  * simulating simple_system code with Spike, which requires the address to be
18:  * 64-bit aligned.
19:  *
20:  */
21: 
22: module simulator_ctrl #(
23:   // passed to simulator via log_name of output_char DPI call
24:   parameter string LogName = "ibex_out.log",
25:   // If set flush on every char (useful for monitoring output whilst
26:   // simulation is running).
27:   parameter bit    FlushOnChar = 1
28: ) (
29:   input               clk_i,
30:   input               rst_ni,
31: 
32:   input               req_i,
33:   input               we_i,
34:   input        [ 3:0] be_i,
35:   input        [31:0] addr_i,
36:   input        [31:0] wdata_i,
37:   output logic        rvalid_o,
38:   output logic [31:0] rdata_o
39: );
40: 
41:   localparam logic [7:0] CHAR_OUT_ADDR = 8'h0;
42:   localparam logic [7:0] SIM_CTRL_ADDR = 8'h2;
43: 
44:   logic [7:0] ctrl_addr;
45:   logic [2:0] sim_finish;
46: 
47:   integer log_fd;
48: 
49:   initial begin
50:     log_fd = $fopen(LogName, "w");
51:   end
52: 
53:   final begin
54:     $fclose(log_fd);
55:   end

57:   assign ctrl_addr = addr_i[9:2];
58:

60:     if (~rst_ni) begin
61:       rvalid_o <= 0;
62:       sim_finish <= 'b0;

Let me summarize what I know:

## Architecture (from README and core files):

**Ibex is a 2-stage or 3-stage pipeline:**
- IF (Instruction Fetch) → ID/EX (Instruction Decode/Execute) → WB (Writeback, optional third stage)
- With optional BranchTargetALU for faster branches

**Module hierarchy:**
```
ibex_top
  ibex_core
    ibex_if_stage (instruction fetch)
      ibex_icache / ibex_prefetch_buffer
      ibex_fetch_fifo
    ibex_id_stage (instruction decode/execute)
      ibex_decoder (decodes 32-bit instructions → control signals)
      ibex_compressed_decoder (expands RVC compressed instructions → 32-bit)
      ibex_controller (pipeline hazard controller)
      ibex_ex_block (execution block)
        ibex_alu (arithmetic/logic/bit manipulation unit)
        ibex_multdiv_fast / ibex_multdiv_slow (multiplier/divider)
      ibex_load_store_unit (load/store address generation)
      ibex_wb_stage (writeback stage, optional)
    ibex_cs_registers (CSR register file)
      ibex_csr (single CSR register)
      ibex_counter (performance/cycle counter)
      ibex_pmp (physical memory protection)
    ibex_branch_predict (static branch predictor)
    ibex_dummy_instr (security hardening)
